title: TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours: Drawing Remote Support Sessions
content:
For every remote support session drawn from a TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours block, and only for a remote session, the minutes drawn and the block hours are figured under the remote-session pricing; a service visit, an installation visit, a project time line and a travel entry keep their own minutes rules and are figured under their own schedules, and every other draw keeps the standard conversion.

A ticket's remote labor is drawn once, when the service desk resolves the ticket, as one remote-support draw dated the resolution's date.

**Band recorded.** For a remote session the band is read from the service desk's resolution of the session's ticket: holiday when the resolution falls on a Saturday or Sunday, emergency for a weekday emergency call-out, after-hours for any other weekday session the desk resolved in the after-hours class, and business hours otherwise, a weekday observed holiday taking the band the resolution's class gives. Every other draw that is not a service visit, an installation visit, a project time line or a travel entry keeps the standard time band.

The draw lowers the block's remaining hours and appears on the block's hours statement.

## Drawing a remote session: `post_remote_session_draw_4c084c45`

**Capability.** Draws the block hours of one remote support session from a TimeBank block: one remote-support draw is added to the block's hours ledger for the given service desk ticket and date, and the block's remaining hours go down by the hours drawn. The client sees the session on the block's hours statement and the lower remaining balance.

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `timebank_block_id` | Reference number of the TimeBank block the session is drawn from, as returned by the TimeBank block lookup. |
| `ticket_number` | The service desk ticket the session was worked on, SB- followed by 7 digits, as shown on the ticket record. |
| `entry_date` | The date of the session, YYYY-MM-DD, US Eastern calendar date. |
| `time_band` | The band the draw is recorded in: `business_hours` records a draw priced at a multiplier of one; `after_hours` records a draw priced at the block's after-hours multiplier; `emergency` records an emergency call-out priced with the block's emergency multiplier; `holiday` records weekend or holiday work priced at the block's holiday multiplier; `not_applicable` is never used for a work draw and is listed only because the ledger carries it for other entries. |
| `resource_level` | The level the session is drawn at: `technician` records a draw at the technician ratio; `senior_engineer` records a draw at the senior engineer ratio; `architect` records a draw at the solutions architect ratio; `not_applicable` is never used for a work draw. |
| `worked_minutes` | The minutes the session is drawn for after rounding and any floor, integer minutes. |
| `hours` | The block hours the session draws, 2 decimal places, rounded half up before it is passed. |

**Return.** `ledger_entry_reference` (reference of the new draw), `block_reference` (the block drawn from), `ticket_number`, `entry_date`, `hours` and `hours_balance_after` (the block's remaining hours after the draw, 2 decimal places). The `ledger_entry_reference` confirms the draw.
